name: How do costs for ground-up construction compare to a major whole-home remodel or addition?

mainEntity.name: How do costs for ground-up construction compare to a major whole-home remodel or addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Costs for ground-up construction often involve acquiring land, extensive site work, and building all systems and structures from scratch, which can sometimes exceed the cost per square foot of a remodel. A major whole-home remodel or addition, however, often faces challenges like integrating new structures with existing ones, or uncovering unforeseen issues within older homes, potentially increasing complexity and costs. When deciding between ground-up construction and a substantial renovation, consider the long-term value, your specific space needs, and the desire for a completely customized home versus optimizing an existing structure.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ground-up construction costs involve land and full new builds, potentially exceeding per-square-foot remodel costs. Remodels can have hidden complexities. Consider long-term value and customization needs.
